class.name: JarVoxelVolume
class.brief_description: A smooth voxel volume: terrain, a planet, a moon or a prop, defined by a signed distance field.
class.description: JarVoxelVolume samples [member sdf] into an octree and meshes it into chunks with level of detail. Everything happens in the volume's local space, so a volume can be moved, rotated and animated freely (for example a moon orbiting a planet), and any number of volumes can exist in one scene. All volumes share one worker thread pool. Level of detail follows every [JarVoxelViewer] in the scene (or the active camera if there is none). Edit the volume with [method sphere_edit] or [method modify]; edits are queued and applied on a background thread. To find the volume behind a physics hit, use [method JarVoxelChunk.get_volume] on the collider's chunk.

method.name: edit
method.description: Combines [param sdf], placed with the global [param transform] (position, rotation and uniform scale), with the volume using [param operation]. The affected region is derived from [method JarSignedDistanceField.get_bounds], so the SDF must be bounded. [param material] (an index into [member materials]) is painted onto changed voxels; the default [code]-1[/code] keeps the existing materials (dug ground then shows the ground rules, and details keep growing on it). [param smoothness] is the blend radius of the smooth operations; [code]0[/code] uses the voxel size. Edits are queued and applied on a background thread. [codeblock] var box := JarBoxSdf.new() box.extent = Vector3(2, 4, 2) volume.edit(box, JarVoxelVolume.SDF_OPERATION_UNION, Transform3D(Basis(Vector3.UP, PI / 4), hit_position)) [/codeblock]

method.name: force_update_lod
method.description: Rebuilds the level of detail around the current viewers as soon as the volume is idle, even if they moved less than [member lod_automatic_update_distance]. Call it after teleporting a viewer.

method.name: get_biome_weights_at
method.description: Returns the biomes present at [param global_position] as a dictionary of [JarBiome] to weight (weights sum to 1). Empty without a [member population_biome_map].

method.name: get_features_near
method.description: Returns the features whose base lies within [param radius] of [param global_position], as dictionaries with [code]feature[/code] (the [JarTerrainFeature]) and [code]transform[/code] (global [Transform3D]). Only generated features (near viewers) are listed.

method.name: get_height_at
method.description: Returns the height of [param global_position] above [member sea_level], measured along the volume's up direction (see [member up_mode]).

method.name: get_runtime_material
method.description: Returns the material the chunks use: the per-volume copy of [member material] (or the default) with the palette filled in. Set shader parameters on it to tweak this volume only at runtime.

method.name: get_up_direction_at
method.description: Returns the global-space up direction at [param global_position] (see [member up_mode]). Useful to orient a character on a planet.

method.name: get_up_field_info
method.description: Returns the up field in effect (see [member up_mode]) as a dictionary in volume-local space: [code]mode[/code] ([constant UP_MODE_AXIS] or [constant UP_MODE_RADIAL]), [code]axis[/code], [code]center[/code] and [code]sea_level[/code] (a height along the axis, or a radius). Water and atmosphere nodes use it.

method.name: is_building
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while the background worker is rebuilding the octree or applying edits. Edits requested meanwhile are queued and applied afterwards.

method.name: is_meshing
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while chunk meshes are queued, being generated, or waiting to be applied. When both this and [method is_building] return [code]false[/code], the terrain around the player is up to date.

method.name: modify
method.description: Modifies the terrain using another [JarSignedDistanceField] instance at a given [code]position[/code], with the specified [code]operation[/code]. The [code]radius[/code] determines the affected area. If [code]sdf[/code] is [code]null[/code], a sphere of [code]radius[/code] is used. [code]material[/code] (an index into [member materials]) is painted onto the affected voxels (see [member material_mode]); pass [code]-1[/code] to keep the existing materials.

method.name: paint
method.description: Paints [param material] (an index into [member materials], 0-254) onto the surface inside [param sdf] (placed by [param transform], like [method edit]) without changing the shape. The weight fades out over one voxel outside the shape, so repeated strokes blend. Each voxel keeps its 4 strongest materials. Painted voxels are kept when level of detail drops.

method.name: raycast_sdf
method.description: Ray marches the volume's base [member sdf] from [param from] to [param to] (global space) and returns [code]{position, normal}[/code] of the first surface hit, or an empty dictionary. Edits are not included. Works at any distance, without colliders: useful for spawning on a planet or aiming far beyond the collider range.

method.name: regenerate_population
method.description: Regenerates all features and details, e.g. after changing their settings at runtime. Removed features stay removed.

method.name: remesh_all
method.description: Remeshes every chunk with the current meshing settings. Called automatically when [member meshing_algorithm], [member dual_contouring_feature_threshold] or [member cubic_voxels] change.

method.name: remove_features
method.description: Removes the features whose base lies within a cube of half size [param radius] around [param global_position], permanently (they are not generated there again). Edits do this automatically for the region they change.

method.name: spawn_debug_spheres_in_bounds
method.description: Spawns debug spheres within the specified [code]range[/code] around [code]position[/code] to visualize terrain bounds or other metrics.

method.name: sphere_edit
method.description: Adds or subtracts a spherical volume from the terrain. The center is defined by [code]position[/code], and [code]radius[/code] defines its size. Set [code]union[/code] to [code]true[/code] to add, or [code]false[/code] to subtract. [code]material[/code] (an index into [member materials]) selects the material painted onto the edited voxels (see [method modify]); pass [code]-1[/code] to keep the existing material.

method.name: update_materials
method.description: Rebuilds the runtime material (palette and texture arrays) before the next frame. Changes to [member materials] and its resources do this automatically.

members.member: Scene used for singular chunk. Will be duplicated once for each rendered chunk.

Physics layers the chunk colliders are on. Putting terrain on its own layer lets areas ignore it: a gravity [Area3D] that moves with a volume (an orbiting moon) and overlaps its terrain colliders costs a lot of physics time every frame, so give such areas a [member CollisionObject3D.collision_mask] without the terrain layer.
Physics layers the chunk colliders scan. Static terrain rarely needs to detect anything itself.
Renders voxels as cubes.

How eagerly dual contouring snaps vertices to sharp features, as a fraction of the strongest surface direction in a cell. Lower values sharpen subtler creases but can add noise on curved surfaces; higher values behave more like surface nets.
If [code]true[/code], the editor preview builds chunk and feature colliders too (needed only for physics in the editor).
If [code]true[/code], the editor preview shows details (grass...). Only while previewing; the game uses [member population_details_enabled].

If [code]true[/code], the volume builds and shows its terrain in the editor, around the editor's 3D camera (otherwise it only runs in the game), with the other [code]editor_preview_*[/code] settings. The generated chunks and population are not saved with the scene. Turning it off frees them.
If [code]true[/code], the editor preview shows features (trees, rocks...). Only while previewing; the game uses [member population_features_enabled].
Finest level of detail the editor preview builds: [code]0[/code] is full detail; each level up halves the resolution (and costs about a quarter as much near the camera).

Edge length, in meters, of the cube the volume covers (centered on the volume's origin). Make it larger than the shape, e.g. at least twice the radius plus the noise height for a planet. Together with [member voxel_size] this sets the octree depth. Applied when the volume enters the tree.
Enables/disables automatic LOD updates when a [JarVoxelViewer] moves.
Distance in world units used to determine whether LODs need to be updated based on player movement.
Extra distance, in meters, around each viewer that is kept at full detail before the levels of detail start to fall off.

How quickly detail falls off: each level of detail is a ring this many chunks (of that level) wide. 1 falls off fastest; larger values keep more detail at a distance. Neighbouring chunks never differ by more than one level, whatever the value.

If [code]true[/code], every separate piece of surface inside a voxel gets its own vertex (with either mesher), so thin walls and features smaller than a voxel stay closed and 2-manifold instead of collapsing into a single vertex. Can be changed at runtime; all chunks are then remeshed.

Material for all chunks of this volume. Empty uses the default material of [member material_mode] ([code]addons/jar_voxel_terrain/materials/terrain_*.tres[/code]). The volume makes a copy per volume and fills in its materials: [code]jar_palette[/code], [code]jar_albedo_textures[/code], [code]jar_normal_textures[/code], [code]jar_has_albedo_textures[/code], [code]jar_has_normal_textures[/code] and [code]jar_material_count[/code]. Each chunk passes [code]jar_chunk_origin[/code], [code]jar_up_center[/code] and [code]jar_up_axis[/code] as instance uniforms. Write your own shader by including [code]terrain_common.gdshaderinc[/code] (see the default shaders) or by declaring those inputs.

How voxel materials reach the shader. [constant MATERIAL_MODE_WEIGHTS]: materials 0-7 blend smoothly (cheapest shader). [constant MATERIAL_MODE_SPLIT]: one material per triangle, crisp borders, up to 255 materials. [constant MATERIAL_MODE_INDEXED]: per triangle the 4 strongest of up to 255 materials, blended smoothly. Unpainted ground is covered by the shader's ground rules in every mode. Can be changed at runtime; all chunks are then remeshed.
[JarTerrainMaterial]s of this volume; the index is the material id. Empty uses a built-in set: 0 grass, 1 rock, 2 sand, 3 seabed, 4 snow (the default ground rules), 5 dirt, 6 dark stone, 7 clay.

How chunks are turned into triangles. [constant MESHING_SURFACE_NETS] gives smooth, rounded surfaces; [constant MESHING_DUAL_CONTOURING] reproduces sharp edges and corners (stamped boxes, meshes, carved tunnels). Can be changed at runtime; all chunks are then remeshed.

Main-thread time per frame, in milliseconds, spent uploading chunk colliders to the physics engine. Colliders nearest the player are uploaded first. Higher values make collision available sooner after the terrain changes, at the cost of frame time.

When greater than [code]0.0[/code], physics colliders are only generated for chunks within this distance of the camera, on top of the usual LOD-based collider rules. Since collider generation is one of the most expensive parts of chunk updates, this can be a large performance win. Set it comfortably larger than the range at which physics interactions are needed. [code]0.0[/code] disables the distance cull (original behaviour).
Optional hard cap on how many chunk colliders are uploaded per second. [code]0[/code] means no cap: uploads are limited only by [member performance_collider_budget_ms].

Biomes of this volume: each biome adds its own features and details where it occurs, and its own ground materials in the terrain shader. The volume's own [member population_terrain_features] and [member population_terrain_details] grow everywhere.
If [code]false[/code], no details are generated or shown (they disappear at once). Turning them back on remeshes the volume to bring them back.
Edge length in meters of the cells features are generated in. Smaller cells follow the surface more closely and stream in finer steps; larger cells mean fewer, bigger jobs and nodes.
If [code]false[/code], no features are generated or shown, including the [JarBiome] features of [member population_biome_map]. Removed features stay removed when they come back.
[JarTerrainDetail]s scattered over full-detail chunks: grass, pebbles, small plants.
[JarTerrainFeature]s placed on the surface around viewers: trees, rocks, structures.
The signed distance field ([JarSignedDistanceField]) used to define terrain shape.
Height 0 for [method get_height_at] and population height ranges: the planet radius for [constant UP_MODE_RADIAL], or the offset along [member up_axis] for [constant UP_MODE_AXIS].
Local up direction when [member up_mode] is [constant UP_MODE_AXIS]; also the fallback at the exact center of a radial volume.
Local-space center: the planet center for [constant UP_MODE_RADIAL], and the origin of height measurement for [constant UP_MODE_AXIS].

Which way is up in this volume, used by the terrain material, population rules, water, atmosphere and player controllers. [constant UP_MODE_AUTO] (default) takes it from the [member sdf] when the SDF knows (a [JarTerrainSdf]: radial for planets, +Y for flat terrain, including its sea level) and otherwise uses +Y. [constant UP_MODE_AXIS] and [constant UP_MODE_RADIAL] use [member up_axis], [member up_center] and [member sea_level].

Edge length of a voxel at full detail (LOD 0), in meters: the smallest feature and edit the volume can represent. Halving it doubles the detail near viewers and costs roughly 8 times more work there. Applied when the volume enters the tree.

constants.constant: Materials 0-7 as 8 smooth blend weights per vertex (vertex [code]COLOR[/code] = materials 0-3, [code]CUSTOM0[/code] = 4-7).
One material per triangle ([code]CUSTOM0.r[/code], 255 = ground), vertices duplicated where materials meet: crisp borders, up to 255 materials.
Per triangle the 4 strongest of up to 255 materials (ids in [code]CUSTOM0[/code], weights in [code]COLOR[/code]); vertices are duplicated where the id sets differ, so blends have no seams.
Smooth surfaces: each vertex sits at the average of its cell's surface crossings.

Sharp features: each vertex is placed where the surface's tangent planes in its cell meet. Edited voxels store the exact surface normal of the edit for this; untouched voxels use the volume SDF's gradient.
Up is the constant [member up_axis] (flat worlds).
Up points away from [member up_center] (planets and moons).
Up direction and sea level come from the [member sdf] (a [JarTerrainSdf]); +Y if the SDF does not define them.
Carves the shape out of the volume.
Keeps only the part of the volume inside the shape.
Adds the shape with a smooth fillet of radius [code]smoothness[/code].
Carves the shape with smoothly rounded edges.
